claim: Let \(T_n=L(K_n)\) be the triangular graph for \(n\ge3\), and let \(\mathcal N(T_n)\) be its Lovász neighborhood complex. For \(3\le n\le6\), the reduced mod-two homology of \(\mathcal N(T_n)\) is nonzero in exactly one degree: \(\widetilde H_1(\mathcal N(T_3);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2\), \(\widetilde H_1(\mathcal N(T_4);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2\), \(\widetilde H_3(\mathcal N(T_5);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^{11}\), and \(\widetilde H_3(\mathcal N(T_6);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^{91}\). At \(n=7\), mixed-dimensional homology appears for the first time: \(\widetilde H_3(\mathcal N(T_7);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^{246}\) and \(\widetilde H_4(\mathcal N(T_7);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^{7}\), with all other reduced mod-two homology groups zero.

correctness.rationale: For each \(n\in\{3,4,5,6,7\}\), the verifier constructs \(T_n\) from the two-subsets of \([n]\), generates every simplex of the neighborhood complex from the open neighborhoods, and reduces every simplicial boundary matrix exactly over \(\mathbf F_2\). The computed Betti vectors are \((1,1)\), \((1,1,0,0)\), \((1,0,0,11,0,0)\), \((1,0,0,91,0,0,0,0)\), and \((1,0,0,246,7,0,0,0,0,0)\). Euler characteristic is independently checked from face counts and homology. Because all smaller \(n\ge3\) are included, \(n=7\) is rigorously the first mixed-dimensional case.

value.rationale: Triangular graphs \(L(K_n)\) are a canonical infinite strongly regular line-graph family. The first appearance of neighborhood homology in two dimensions is a natural structural threshold, and the exact ranks \(246\) and \(7\) provide a nontrivial benchmark for general theories of neighborhood/Hom complexes. The result is not an arbitrary finite slice: it identifies the earliest parameter where the qualitative homology pattern changes.
